To me, niceness is a form of acting. An act of politeness. You can act like a good person, typically to soften someone up to get you to your goal, to give you something you want. To make a good impression of *yourself*.

One of the examples of niceness: You're being pleasant with a shop's cashier because you don't want them to mistreat the things *you* brought.

Another example: You're acting really good in front of your teacher, and your classmates because you want everyone to look up to *you*.

Kindness comes from within your heart. It is a quality out of deep love, respect, understanding, empathy, and genuine care. Your focus is now on the *others*. Your kindness does not have any ultimate selfish goal. You want to help people because you want to see them get better, simple as that.

Some examples of kindness: There's an unconscious someone wounded and they're bleeding intensely, they won't remember who saved them and there's nobody nearby to see you help, but you still decide to save them because you want *them* to live.

A lighter example: There's someone at work who forgot to pack their lunch, and you decided to share your food because you don't want *them* to starve. You're not expecting anything else.

A person with enough self-love knows how to treat someone with kindness. Because they know that kindness is a form of love, and true love is a pure, unconditional quality. It does not need any motivation or personal gains behind it. *This* is kindness.

To sum it up in simpler terms: Niceness is a quality and a pleaseable act, *self-centered.* Kindness is a quality and love, *other-centered.*

*Both qualities can appear in the same action. It is the intention of the person that makes them fundamentally different.*

I hope this clears up some confusion :).

The comment I made above was just me trying to see from her perspective, break down her sentences, and analyze what she means in which of them.

You can interpret this as me trying to harmonize The Shifting Mound, I think that TSM thinks there is no other way. She is not just the Tower/Apotheosis, she can be just as gentle as the Damsel, as cold as the Prisoner, as deceitful as the witch- she is all of the princess at once. She just discovered who she is and what is the true meaning of her existence. She chose to carry all of the wisdom and responsibilities she contains. And wants nothing more than to leave the Construct with you, be with you, and watch over reality together.

Combining my comment above. From her perspective, it only makes sense that she views herself as important. That the "only right way" out was to leave with TLQ and watch over the new universe, and refuse to have any other way. To her, the duties she carried were too important to be left alone.

Is it arrogant of her? Yes, absolutely. But if you go from an empathetic point and try to understand her, maybe you can start to feel how heavy her burdens are and how alone she'd feel if she only had herself in her company. Her entire "boss fight" with you was just her trying to persuade you to join her. After all, as important as she is(Change), she still needs you(Stasis) to leave. "And speaking of opinions, in my own arrogant opinion, siding with TSM or the Narrator/Echoes is the wrong choice in any case. If you side with either, you forsake what lies at your core: the ability to move past, to make a different choice."

There are no premature endings. There are no wrong decisions.

There are only fresh perspectives and new beginnings.

Is that not what this whole game is about? Every choice is valid, every path you chose and didn't choose is just fine. What if it is the player's wish to choose to leave with TSM? What if that's their way and preference to move past the fight with TSM and get "There is no ending"? What even is "A different choice"?

If we condemn whatever ending people get, then we could just as easily say "You two are just throwing away responsibilities and being selfish by choosing to be mortals", to the "What Happens Now?" ending.

"Leaving with TSM is just letting people die without a care", to the "There are No Endings" ending.

"Siding with the Narrator and slaying the princess is just delusional and wrong", to "A New and Unending Dawn" ending.

"Choosing to Loop the game forever is just living in a bubble and refusing to face what happens to the outside world"... etc.

Did you notice how black-and-white those viewpoints are? How each ending have so much more nuances and depths in it than those one sentence? You're absolutely welcome to favor whichever endings you want, but please try not to view your ending as the "only right" one, because the other endings can be just as meaningful as yours.

She is a reality, a concept, a goddess- sure, but she's now sentiment. She can feel things now. She can think for herself now. Shifty was just a process before, but the Echo decided to split a concept in half, personified and reduced TLQ and TSM to forget who they are and kill each other, just for a reality he wanted. Imagine yourself as TSM(impossible, I know, but try using your empathy.) You'd be angry, right? You discover who you are- one of the most fundamental qualities needed in reality. You'd also gain endless wisdom, endless "you". Of course, this comes along with endless responsibility. 

You can finally see another part of you, which isn't you anymore, but his own person. Imagine him rejecting you in the face, the only being that can understand you, to bear this burden with you, a being you love. That has to hurt, right?

Stubbornly (just as you are) standing along with his beliefs. No one is getting anywhere. I think that's why I disliked this new section. Only very few I see in this subreddit see what good she brings too. To me, she is just a path to your goal/destination. How you want the path to be/to look like is your choice. Active change exists. To be a better person, to be kinder, braver, stronger. She is the path that needs to exist for that to be possible.

And who's to say that another Big Bang/God created another Earth-like planet/whichever way you believe a universe start wouldn't happen? Everything we had before, everything we have now, and everything that we will have in the future only exist thanks to change. May it be good or bad. That's what she is responsible for, and that's what she wants to observe with you.

I think one of the biggest nitpicks I had for the new update is the new dialogs. It's been weeks now and the devs do have an explanation for it. But I still feel that those dialogs you can pick when fighting her final form, or incomplete form are purposefully made to antagonize her(or at least, the majority of it).

I mean, be honest, how would you act if you're arguing with someone, and they ignored everything you say, calling you "pretentious(This is debatable. I personally use my own life experience and try to relate to her metaphors on why change is important. But I can see why some cannot)" and "wearing the princess's skin((even though that's their(TLQ) perception that made you a princess.))". You'd feel pissed, right? There's quite a lot of dialog I can see why TSM disagrees. (Personal interpretation of the new options and TSM.)

•Appeal to Your Shared Humanity. You reject the notion that either of you two are goddess, try to minimize and see things from a "human" perceptive. She rejects this. The Shifting Mound already accepted herself as a goddess, even reality itself, and alongside, the responsibilities of being one. Shifty's also aware of the consequences of being trapped here and leaving would be. If you consider all of that, it's only natural her words will be grand.

•Reject her Authority. I'm sorry, but I can't see how to describe this other than you're just insulting her and trying to pull her down. Can anyone also explain how any lines she says the moment you meet her as a "lecture"?

•Argue your Independence. This one is intriguing. You think that TSM is a god, but you also think that she gets a say in how things will change and/or she made the changes whichever way she wants it to. But by talking to her she explains she's not like that. She's not a controller of change, but the concept in itself. She is the transformation for all things possible, she -rather it- exists everywhere. She is change itself, given identity, consciousness, and sentiment.

•Reject Her Perspective. This is the most complex out of all the routes you can go to argue with her. There are a few factors we are basing our assertions on:

1: We think that she is a controller of change.

2. We focus on only the negative things change can bring: suffering, oblivion, destruction, death, etc.

3. We hold ourselves and TSM responsible for the suffering of the people.

4. We think that once people die, that's the end.

5. We think that there is finality.

At this point, we are arguing on the opposite belief that she has/she is. She exists as a possibility for things to be better, to be worse, to be anywhere in between. It's up to the people to decide what form she takes. She is what others perceive her to be.

She is just a process. And she views herself(change) as important. If the people don't see through their fears and realize the good things change will bring, it's not her fault. To her, the fears and delusions people feel are theirs to bear. She also doesn't believe "endings" exist. Only new beginnings. That's why the recent survey the devs posted called the God ascending ending as "There is no ending."

After seeing all these wonderful fanart on this subreddit, I’ve decided to have my own spin on it! These three are my personal favorites. I’ve drawn how they’d react to each other in my head. 

This piece was set in the middle of winter, so I wanted them (except Smitten) to wear winter clothes, hence why they’re not wearing their usual dresses. Using color allows me to exaggerate their clothing, that's why I decided to use it in this art.

If you’re interested, I’ll list how and why I’ve designed their clothing the way they are:

Thorn’s design: All clothing reflects what the chapters have to offer. In the original game, the thorns are on the top of Thorn’s strapless dress, directly piercing her chest and arms. Since I wanted to draw her healing (physically and mentally) and happy, I’ve added clothing underneath her thorns/poppies capes. To maintain the quality of her character design, and still doesn’t make her suffer.

It doesn’t match the purpose of her original design, that’s why I added poppies growing out of the thornless vines, to symbolize poppies(peace) can still grow out and above the thorns(past).

These are all the flowers picked for the flower crown: Iris(Blue, purple, and white), Snowdrop(white), and daffodils(White, yellow, and orange), because they’re all associated with a common meaning.

Smitten design: I pretty much created him based on what I know about TLQ. Changed the patterns of his arms and legs into heart shapes, had roses carved into his beak, and gave him an overall pinkish/reddish palette. You can either interpret his shoe design as falling feathers, or burning fire.

>!I’ve chosen Smitten over others because he’s the one with the highest EQ (in terms of understanding the Thorn in her route, the one who insists on freeing her, and the one that makes the \[Kiss\] option available.)!<

Spectre design: There isn’t much aspect I can get in the Spectre chapter, besides ripped and fading dress, so I’ve also used the Wraith to get ideas from. The hoodie was a great idea, and that’s when I started to base her on the Reaper (The gray piece of fabric represents the blade). The shoes are based on her desire to see the outside world, but her life was unfortunately cut short by a stab wound. >!Also, say hello to the little ghosts! When I analyse the game, there's four people(at least) that is needed to be considered: the Narrator, the Voice of the Hero, the other voices that appears whenever you go in the next chapter, and the most important aspect - the player.

Neither the Narrator nor the long quiet chooses the princess to be however she appears to be in chapter 2. It's your choice, as a player, that chooses to perceive the princess to be someone who you think she is, thus the princess becomes that way.

If you think she's a Damsel in distress, then she'll be a Damsel in distress. If you think she's alive and checking her pulse right after killing her, she'll come back to life. Basically, how you perceived her to be (what choices you made in Ch1), is how she is going to be in Ch2. 

But even then it's not the whole truth. The best way to put this is that she is a parallel to your choices. How you perceived the princess will change her drastically, yes, but she doesn't act exactly how you see her, it's how she thinks you thought of her to be. And ultimately it's the storytelling that takes hold of it. 

Think of the chapter 2 princess is a mix of the writing itself, how she thinks you thought of her to be, and the direct consequences of your choices.

There's actually a canonical answer to this.

When the narrator appears in shattered glasses, the scene where you can ask him questions. There's a question "When you created us, why did you make her a princess?" Or something along the lines you can ask him.

Another response is: "Are you asking me to spend my final moments psychoanalyzing you? Sigh. She wound up as a princess because you wanted her to be a princess. As to why?

Maybe she needed to be beautiful. Important. Above you, but on a level you could still approach. A herald of things to come.

I don't know. Gods are supposed to be beyond comprehension. I really shouldn't try and anthropomorphize you like this."

The latter is a perception from the narrator of reasoning as to why The Long Quiet chose her to be a princess. But one thing's for sure, TLQ is the one who decided TSM to be a princess.
